Seventh:
no man from a thousand, or a hundred, or a ten to which he was numbered, shall move to another place;
otherwise, he shall be killed, as well as the leader who received him.
Eighth:
from every two ten thousands (tumens), horses shall be set in order along the road for the riding of envoys.
Ninth:
from a dead person who has no heir, nothing shall be taken for the king;
rather, to the one who used to serve him his possessions shall be given, and even his wife.
For they have many other laws,
and so as not to be tedious,
a portion of {OCR?} them we have not mentioned.
Concerning how they adhered to the worship of idols: for the Mongols, indeed, previously had neither a script nor a distinct religion,
but they only knew one God, the Creator of all,
and some of them confessed and called upon the God of heaven,
until they gained dominion over the people of the mountain Turks,
and they found that there were sorcerers among them, those who are called Qams (shamans).
And we have heard many who testify about them and say:
"We have heard the voice of demons speaking with them from the corners of the tent curtains."
And this initiation of theirs from the demons is not accomplished
except after they are defiled by other men,
because most of them are effeminate men (catamites).
And all of this is abominable,
for when they wish to perform something of their sorcery,
whomever they meet,
they seize by force to defile them.
Therefore, when the Mongols saw them,
they too inclined after them in their simplicity.
Afterwards, Genghis Khan heard
that the Chinese, who are the Cathayans, have idols and priests possessing wisdom.
He sent envoys to them,
and demanded priests from them,
and promised that he would hold them in honor.
And when the priests came,
Genghis Khan commanded
that the priests make a debate and examination concerning religion with the Qams.
And when the priests spoke and read something from their book,
which they call "Nom" in their language,
the Qams were defeated and vanquished,
and they were not able to utter a word,
because they were destitute of knowledge.
